A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SeedVR and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and supplementary Sections 6–7. Corresponding material can be reliably matched across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original restoration evaluations on six benchmarks, VAE reconstruction comparisons, and window-size performance and timing experiments in Tables 1–4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical studies, revises baseline results, and adds a CV-VAE reconstruction comparison.

M1.justification: The shifted-window transformer, 3D positional embeddings, causal video VAE, conditioning procedures, and progressive training strategy are unchanged. Supplementary Section 7 retains the same window-level text interaction and averaging procedure; terminology edits do not change the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use mixed image/video training and evaluate SPMCS, UDM10, REDS30, YouHQ40, VideoLQ, and AIGC38. The qualitative scenes are retained. The revised training-image count changes sample size, without establishing different task or population coverage.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds CV-VAE (SD3) as a reconstruction comparator while retaining all previous VAE baselines. Table 1's restoration comparator membership is unchanged; Upscale-A-Video receives revised scores rather than being added or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 3.3 revises the reported training corpus from approximately 100 million images to 10 million, retaining 5 million videos. This tenfold revision substantially changes the stated training scale, although the PDFs do not establish whether it corrects documentation or reflects retraining. The reported evaluation resolutions, metrics, and window-study settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Figures 1 and 4 revise the qualitative detail-recovery comparisons by replacing Upscale-A-Video outputs for the same scenes, changing the visual evidence about recovered textures. The window-size sensitivity and efficiency studies in Tables 3–4 are unchanged, with no new robustness or failure scenarios.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run variability, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Both present point estimates using the same reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces all 40 Upscale-A-Video scores across six benchmarks, materially changing its relative standing. For example, AIGC38 DOVER changes from 10.297 to 12.857, placing it second, and VideoLQ NIQE changes from 5.545 to 3.490, overtaking SeedVR's unchanged 3.874. SeedVR and the other Table 1 methods retain their scores. Table 2 adds CV-VAE results, including LPIPS 0.0589 and rFVD 6.50; qualitative baseline outputs also change.

T1.justification: The tensor and attention definitions, window-partition expressions, conditioning-noise equation, and supplementary shared-text assumption are retained. No mathematical derivation, formal property, or proof is added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and scope: arbitrary-length/resolution restoration, a scalable diffusion transformer with a causal VAE, competitive restoration quality, and over twice the speed of existing diffusion-based video restoration methods.

C2.justification: Section 4.1 qualifies SeedVR's metric performance from 'the best' to 'high' DISTS, LPIPS, NIQE, and DOVER scores. Section 3.3 attributes degradation diversity to applying diverse degradations at scale rather than to precomputation itself. Existing fidelity tradeoffs and window-size interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Section 4 explicitly identifies Upscale-A-Video as the source followed for synthesizing training pairs, refining v1's grouped degradation-method citations in Section 3.3. This clarifies documentation without establishing a changed synthesis procedure. Hardware, training budgets, the supplementary VEnhancer checkpoint disclosure, and project access information are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Zhao et al.'s CV-VAE paper and cites it for the new Table 2 comparator. The related-work discussion and broader novelty positioning are otherwise retained; subsequent reference-number changes reflect this insertion.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes terminology such as MMDiT, Swin-MMDiT, and NaViT, makes limited grammatical edits including in the supplement, adds Fei Xiao to the author list, and shortens the funding acknowledgment. The section organization and overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 1 and 4 update qualitative comparison crops while retaining their scenes and panel arrangements. Table 2 gains a CV-VAE row, and architecture figures receive terminology edits. There is no substantial figure redesign or document-layout reorganization.

improvement.justification: The added VAE comparator, clearer synthesis attribution, and qualified metric wording provide limited benefits. However, the training-image-count revision and replaced Upscale-A-Video results are unexplained. Figure 1 retains v1's Upscale-A-Video DOVER point near 10.3, whereas v3's Table 1 reports 12.857 on AIGC38, without identifying different scoring conditions. These unresolved reporting issues prevent a reliable judgment that the changes produce a net improvement in paper quality.
